blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: She was recovering, she had not recovered, which is the natural history of pneumonia.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: Yes. In your report that you wrote, and the one that you were taken to, the second of the reports, it's dated 31 May 2018, paragraph 44, you say that there was a window of near complete recovery. There's a difference, isn't there, between recovering and recovery; would you agree?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "Near complete recovery", quite happy to use that, or use the word recovering. I think this is semantics.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: Perfectly happy to run with either observation.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: I'm going to suggest to you, the fact is [Baby D] was not anywhere near to a complete recovery, was she?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: She was recovering.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: Right. If she's recovering, that means she still has the potential to become quite unwell, doesn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: She's in a neonatal unit, the best place for her on the planet. If she was becoming unwell as a result of infection, she would have had -- she was on full monitoring, she had nurses all round her, she had doctors round the corner, as it were, and we -- and we recognise, doctors and nurses on neonatal units, we recognise clinical characteristics that would indicate she is not as well as she was or she's getting worse.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: She showed none of those just prior to 1.30 in the morning.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: What I asked was if she is recovering, as opposed to being in a state of recovery. If she's recovering that means she still has the potential to deteriorate and become quite unwell, doesn't she?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: So if she doesn't cope without CPAP, they might find a drop in — her breathing might increase or her heart rate might increase or her oxygen requirement might go up a bit or her oxygen saturation might drop to the low 90s. You know, I am just saying these are the sort of things that any experienced nurse would look for. So therefore let's try her.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: What would not happen -- what would not happen -- let me be absolutely clear about this: what would not happen in a baby of 37 weeks, who is recovering from pneumonia, you take her off CPAP, she wouldn't suddenly crash and where resuscitation, including adrenaline, et cetera, was unsuccessful. That does not -- that is not a clinical process that anybody dealing with babies of this nature see. Whereas if she received a bolus of air intravenously, then we're back to my diagnosis of air embolus, which is what happened in this case. Okay?
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: And your evidence on that is that if she receives a bolus of air intravenously, one of the features that gets top billing in your list, Dr Evans, is the presence of discolouration. You have been very clear about that.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: It's not top billing at all. I've explained to you the five steps, one of which is this discolouration.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: It was second, you said. First is the unexpected collapse. The second is discolouration.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: That's the sequence of events, not the order of priority -- of significance.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: As it happens there's no evidence or suggestion of any discolouration at all with the third collapse that we're looking at, is there?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: She collapsed, you know.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: And that is inconsistent with your theory of air embolus, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, it is not. Okay? It is not. Babies collapse, they're doing their best to resuscitate her and they are sadly unsuccessful.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: There's no discolouration on that final occasion, was there?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: As far as I know nothing was recorded anyway.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: And that is inconsistent with the way you've described the presentation of an air embolus, isn't it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, it is not, because what I said earlier was, I described the five criteria and I said you don't need all five to confirm a diagnosis of air embolus. So in [Baby D]'s case we had the collapse, failure of resuscitation -- sorry, and air in the aorta. That's for the radiologists to comment on. And the absence of, you know, anything else really. So yes. So yes, I'll stick with that, I'll stick with that.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: Your evidence on that in conclusion was:
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: "A small volume caused a precipitous deterioration [this is in the report] in the baby's condition and lead to efforts at resuscitation failing and it may explain abdominal discolouration."
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Mm.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: Yes. On the two occasions when we have some abdominal discolouration, resuscitation doesn't fail, does it? Does it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Well, you said earlier she didn't need resuscitation, so you're now admitting that she did have resuscitation, so which one is it, please?
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: On the two occasions when she had discolouration --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Which one is it? Sorry, I am not picking on you, I just need clarification. You made an effort to tell me that she did not require resuscitation on the second event and I said to her (sic), yes, she did, she required 100% oxygen, and now you are trying to tell me she did require resuscitation, so which question are you asking me, please?
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: Well, you understand the point, Dr Evans.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: No, I do not, actually.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: Resuscitative measures that failed do not feature in events 1 and 2, do they? They do not feature.
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: Depends on the -- it depends on the volume of air given intravenously and the rate at which it was given.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: You agree --
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: And I think we'll discuss that in a later case as well, so yes.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: I just want to confirm, taking that sentence to conclude this, you agree that resuscitative efforts did not fail on events 1 and 2, did they?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: She only required resuscitation with oxygen and it was successful.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: And although you talk about the embolus may explain the abdominal discolouration, there is in fact no abdominal discolouration on event number 3, is there?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: There is nothing recorded.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: You suggest they all missed it?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I have no idea, I wasn't there. But if I've got a baby under my care, who's got no chest wall movement, heart rate under 60, you know, I'm not going to start looking at whether she's got a discolouration of her abdomen.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: I'm going to go full pelt to try and save a baby's life, for goodness sake.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: Have you seen any evidence of discolouration on the third event?
blocks.speaker: MYERS

blocks.text: I have just explained to you that I have not seen anything. I have no idea what the significance of that is, but — yes, but this is not what -- yes, anyway.
blocks.speaker: EVANS

blocks.text: Thank you.
blocks.speaker: MR MYERS
